solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dictatorial of the French head, revolting in charge

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' before a plural noun

indicators.note: revolting here means turning over, so the word for head is read backwards

parts.note: the top of something is its head

explanation.surface: A foreign leader rebels against whoever is running things in an autocratic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns TOP into POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant rules absolutely, so behaviour that is tyrannical is synonymous with dictatorial.

clue.text: Food fixed up with insides upset

indicators.note: the two inner letters of the result are turned over as well, swapping their order
in a down clue, up means the word for fixed is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: something tied is fixed in place

explanation.surface: A meal that has been prepared, with the cook's stomach churning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIED into DEIT; 'insides upset' then swaps its middle EI to IE.
explanation.definitionFit: What one regularly eats is one's nourishment, so the word for a regime of meals stands for food.

clue.text: It's unacceptable to hold single belief

indicators.note: to hold means the phrase for unacceptable wraps round the letter for one

parts.note: 'not on' is a British idiom for something unacceptable
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is wrong to cling to one solitary conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT ON, the British phrase for 'unacceptable', holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea someone holds is a view or opinion, close in sense to a belief.

clue.text: Ashamed, and second, rather humble?

parts.note: Uriah Heep in Dickens's David Copperfield is famously 'umble', so being rather like him is Heep-ish

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed, and in second place, feeling fairly modest.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: -ISH means 'rather', added to Heep, the falsely humble clerk in Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed by what they did looks abashed, a synonym of ashamed.

clue.text: Pique irregular case with sex in short supply

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, so the outermost letters are taken
in means the word for sex goes inside the word for limited supply

parts.note: a ration is a limited allowance when goods are scarce
IT is a familiar euphemism for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Annoyance at an odd situation where lovemaking is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' takes the outer letters of 'irregular'; 'in' places the sex inside the scarce supply, giving RITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is resentment at a slight, a kind of annoyance or vexation.

clue.text: Drop exercise taking breather

indicators.note: taking means the letters for exercise take in the organ of breathing

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
a lung is what one breathes with

explanation.surface: Abandon a workout to take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' looks like a rest, but it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fall, as in prices, is both a dive and a drop.

clue.text: Willing English before Lord's in duck, practically

indicators.note: in means the letters for English and Lord sit within the trimmed word for duck
practically means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to duck someone is to plunge them into water, to douse them

indicators.note: before puts the letter for English ahead of the title

parts.note: sir is a form of address, used here for a lord

explanation.surface: A cricketer at Lord's nearly out for nought, keen to bat on.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground and a duck is a score of nought, but here the 's is 'is' and duck is DOUSE, cut to DOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen to have something makes one eager, so wanting and willing are close synonyms.

clue.text: Glorious return of US soldiers nearly odds on

indicators.note: on means the second part follows the first
return means the word for American soldiers is read backwards, upwards in this down entry

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

indicators.note: the odd letters, first, third and fifth, are taken from the word

explanation.surface: A splendid homecoming for American troops, almost a racing certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odds on' looks like the betting phrase; here 'odds' takes N, A, L from 'nearly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable or outstanding victory is called a signal one, so the adjective means striking or glorious.

clue.text: Just Oliver eating last of gruel

indicators.note: eating means the name surrounds the letter taken from the food

parts.note: Oliver Hardy, of the comedy double act Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist barely eating the end of his gruel.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver suggests Twist and his gruel; it is Oliver Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely, scarcely and only just are synonyms, so 'just' fits the adverb.

clue.text: Boil pan on top of stove

indicators.note: on means the cooking vessel is placed next to the first letter
top of means the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a pot is a cooking pan

explanation.surface: Bring a saucepan on the hob to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boil' looks like a cooking verb; it is a noun, a skin blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil is an inflamed lump on the skin, and a pimple or blemish is a spot.

clue.text: Going red I entertained, accepting part

indicators.note: accepting means the run of words takes in the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone blushing as host while agreeing to play a role.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across goING RED I ENTertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A component of a mixture or recipe is one part of the whole.

clue.text: Scattered shot, rifle and weapon emptied

indicators.note: emptied means each word loses its inside letters, leaving only the outer pair

explanation.surface: Spent cartridges lie spread around, the gun and other arms unloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' applies to all three words: ST, RE and WN.
explanation.definitionFit: Things spread untidily over an area have been scattered, the past participle of strew.

clue.text: Care for former wife feeling cold, not tense

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: the clue says cold rather than tense, so one letter for tense is swapped for the letter for cold

parts.note: an attitude is a feeling or stance
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Looking after an ex-wife who feels chilly but not anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold, not tense' changes the first T of ATTITUDE to C.
explanation.definitionFit: Precision and meticulousness are a form of carefulness, so care fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Eager bird flipped boyfriend head to toe

indicators.note: flipped means the bird's name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of myna, the Asian starling

indicators.note: the first letter is moved from the front to the end

parts.note: a date is someone you are seeing romantically

explanation.surface: A keen bird turns somersaults and her boyfriend goes heels over head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' gives ANIM; 'head to toe' moves D of DATE to the end, ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively, spirited and enthusiastic all describe someone keen, so the adjective serves as eager.

clue.text: Vulgarly cheap restaurant's carrying hard ribs

indicators.note: carrying means the word for the eatery holds the letter for hard

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe; the 's supplies the S
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A greasy spoon serving tough spare ribs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ribs' is a verb, to tease; 'ribs' as food is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh or tease someone good-naturedly is to banter, and both words mean ribs as a verb.

clue.text: Sweet female's harangue suppressing anger, oddly

indicators.note: suppressing means the tirade holds down the selected letters inside it

parts.note: a rant is a loud harangue

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A lovely woman's tirade strangely holding back her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes A, G, R from 'anger'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell is described as sweet-smelling or perfumed.

clue.text: Little one's quiet, softly gripping apron

indicators.note: gripping means the letters for quiet and softly close around the edge

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an apron is a border or edge, as of a stage, so a rim

explanation.surface: A small child is silent, gently clutching a pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apron' suggests clothing; it means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is a teasing name for a very small person, a little one.

clue.text: Gasp keeping control, not one with child!

indicators.note: keeping means the word for gasp keeps the next letters inside it

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath

indicators.note: not means the letter for one is removed

parts.note: to reign is to hold control
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A gasp, holding oneself together, as one is not alone but has a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark nods to the surface: being 'not one' fits an expectant mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An expectant mother is carrying a baby, the old phrase with child.

clue.text: Pass is taken, involving support for goal

indicators.note: involving means these words contain the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A pass is accepted, setting up a strike at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across pASS IS Taken.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the pass that sets up a scorer is credited as helping towards the goal.

clue.text: Takes off small pieces with half-naked back

indicators.note: back means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: parts are pieces

indicators.note: half means only the first two of the four letters are kept

parts.note: nude means naked

explanation.surface: Someone undressing removes bits of clothing, baring half their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses S + PARTS + NU (half of NUDE).
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing the belts that hold something on is removing it, so it takes it off.

clue.text: Stress seeing number's up around end of war

indicators.note: around means the number goes round the chosen letter
in a down entry up means the number is read from the bottom

parts.note: seven is a number

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Tension rises as numbers swell near the close of a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVEN round R gives SEVREN; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or strain on the mind is described as an attack of the jitters, synonymous with stress.

clue.text: Heavy vehicle hit side of road, missing tail-end

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: missing tail-end means the last letter of the roadside word is dropped

parts.note: the kerb is the edge of a pavement beside the road (British spelling)

explanation.surface: A lorry crashes into the roadside, its rear jutting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a collision; it is TAN, to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: A large lorry or ship carrying liquid in bulk is a heavy vehicle.

clue.text: Subject of article poses wasting time

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: wasting means the letter for time is lost from the word

parts.note: a model sits or poses for an artist

explanation.surface: The topic of a piece of writing is modelling that wastes time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poses' is a verb here, as a model sits for a painter; 'wasting' drops its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation argues a proposition, and the proposition is the subject of the work.

clue.text: Consort with fellow and bird in lift

indicators.note: in means the seabird goes inside the word for lift

parts.note: to raise is to lift
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Keeping company with a man and a woman in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' as a girlfriend and 'lift' as an elevator both mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix with or associate with someone is to consort with them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Starts to criminally operate nefarious sting

definitions.text: Starts to criminally operate nefarious sting

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The beginnings of a crooked plan to run a wicked swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The four initials spell the word, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindles and confidence tricks are crooked operations, criminal stings.

clue.text: Inexperienced person, inexperienced person in bed

indicators.note: in means the learner letter is placed inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
L, for learner, marks an inexperienced driver

explanation.surface: A novice repeated, a beginner lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase does two jobs: definition, then L for learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A young horse, and by extension a novice or youngster in sport, is a newcomer.

clue.text: Flush endless swirl in unfinished burst

indicators.note: in means the trimmed whirl goes inside the trimmed tear
unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to rend is to tear or burst apart

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: an eddy is a swirl of water

explanation.surface: A toilet flush swirling ceaselessly in a partial eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: EDD goes inside REN.
explanation.definitionFit: To go red in the face is to blush, the sense of flush as a verb.

clue.text: Insignificant affair on short voyage

indicators.note: on means the affair is set next to the shortened journey
short means the word is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a journey or voyage
a fling is a brief affair

explanation.surface: A meaningless romance on a brief cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIP loses P to give TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something petty or of little value is unimportant, a synonym of insignificant.
